questions.q: What is the vernacular term for Solder?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Hinang” = solder. Native Visayan word: hinang means “to work, make”. Memory hook: the tinsmith's work of joining metal.

questions.q: Which vernacular term corresponds to Temper (metalwork)?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
questions.n: “Suban, Subuhal” = temper (metalwork). Native terms; origin not confirmed. Memory hook: suban sounds like “sub-merge”; tempering means plunging hot metal into water or oil to harden it.

questions.q: In Philippine construction vernacular, Wrought iron strap is called:
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
questions.n: “Planchuela / Plantsuwela” = wrought iron strap. Origin: Spanish planchuela “flat bar”, from plancha “plate”. Plantsuwela is the same word spelled differently. The same term is also used for: W.I. strap.

questions.q: What is the vernacular term for Soldering lead?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Estanyo / Estaniyo” = soldering lead. Origin: Spanish estaño “tin”, since solder is largely tin. The same term is also used for: nicolite bar, solder bar.

questions.q: Which vernacular term corresponds to Cast iron?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
questions.n: “Pundido” = cast iron. Origin: Spanish fundido “cast, melted”, from fundir “to melt, cast”. Same root as English “found” (to cast metal).

questions.q: In Philippine construction vernacular, Iron is called:
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Hiero” = iron. Origin: Spanish hierro “iron”, from Latin ferrum, the root of “ferrous”.

questions.q: What is the vernacular term for Nicolite bar?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Estanyo / Estaniyo” = nicolite bar. Origin: Spanish estaño “tin”, since solder is largely tin. The same term is also used for: solder bar, soldering lead.

questions.q: Which vernacular term corresponds to Sheet (metal)?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
questions.n: “Plantsa” = sheet (metal). Origin: Spanish plancha “plate, flat iron”. Plantsa also means to iron clothes: both are flat metal.

questions.q: In Philippine construction vernacular, G.I. strap (plain G.I. strap) is called:
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Lingueta” = G.I. strap (plain G.I. strap). Origin: Spanish lengüeta “little tongue, tab”. A strap is a thin tongue of metal.

questions.q: What is the vernacular term for W.I. strap?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
questions.n: “Planchuela / Plantsuwela” = W.I. strap. Origin: Spanish planchuela “flat bar”, from plancha “plate”. A strap is a flat bar of wrought iron. The same term is also used for: Wrought iron strap.

questions.q: Which vernacular term corresponds to Reinforcing bar?
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Kabilya” = reinforcing bar. Origin: Spanish cabilla “iron rod”, the usual word for rebar in Spanish.

questions.q: In Philippine construction vernacular, Solder bar is called:
questions.ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
questions.n: “Estanyo / Estaniyo” = solder bar. Origin: Spanish estaño “tin”, since solder is largely tin. The same term is also used for: nicolite bar, soldering lead.
